title: Baker v Baker: Jon Takes the Lot
title_candidates: Baker v Baker: Jon Takes the Lot
Forty-Five Holes in Front, and Then His Brother
Two Course Records and a Family Argument
theme: The perennial runner-up finally cashes in: Jon Baker, Jacket bridesmaid in three of the last four TEGs, breaks two course records, holds off his own brother by six, and takes David Mullin's Jacket off him — while Mullin, gross runner-up, ends up holding the Spoon.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register; ribbing aimed at the blow-ups, respect for the winner
opening_hook: Open at El Prat, R3 H13 (b01): Jon Baker, 45 holes in front since R1 H4, makes a routine par and still hands the Trophy lead to his brother Alex — then loop back to how a man who had never won a Jacket got there in the first place.
foreshadow: Jon Baker went in as Jacket runner-up in three of the last four TEGs, with no win; David Mullin arrived with 8 Jacket wins and back-to-back titles.
Jon's R1 90 at the Stadium (cr01) was a new course record and a 9-shot improvement on his last visit — a hint that this was a different Jon.
The 13th at PGA Catalunya - Stadium (SI 6) collecting numbers from the start: Alex Baker's 8 in R1 (b17), Patterson's 9 (b25).
Mullin scoring beautifully in raw shots — new personal bests at both PGA Catalunya courses — while quietly sliding down the Stableford table.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Jon Baker (143 pts, by 6 from Alex Baker)
competitions.how: Jon led from R1 H4 (35 pts) and stretched it with 41 in R2, the best round of the tournament by any measure; he then bled 7 shots in three holes at El Prat (b42) and lost a 45-hole tenure at R3 H13 to Alex (b01/b06), who had crept level at H1 (b40) and gone outright ahead on the back of a level-par run (b35). Two down starting R4, Jon drew level at H6 (b09) — with a double bogey, because Alex was busy dropping 7 shots in three holes (b38) — and never trailed again. Alex's 27 pts (b11), his worst TEG round, turned a two-point lead into a six-point defeat.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Jon Baker (+70, by 3 from David Mullin)
competitions.how: Jon led the gross from R1 H4 and never once finished a round out of first, but it was closer than the leaderboard suggests: a course-record 90 at the Stadium (cr01) and a course-record 84 on the Tour (cr02) built the cushion, Mullin took the lead back at R3 H5 after 37 holes (b02), and Jon reclaimed it outright at R3 H6 (b05) when Mullin ran up a 7 at the same short hole (b18). Mullin drew level again at R4 H3 (b10) off a three-par opening burst (b22), then bled 7 shots from H15 (b39). Jon's own quadruple bogey at the 13th (b16) cost him nothing. First Jacket for Jon; the end of Mullin's back-to-back run.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Patterson looked the obvious candidate, bottom after R1 (from H14, b44) and R2, the latter including an 11 at the 15th (b12) and a new Tour course-worst of 103 (cr03). But Mullin, 4th after two rounds, went 29 and 31 in R3 and R4 and dropped to last at R3 H12 (b21) — a bogey at the easiest hole on the course (SI 18) — after a quadruple bogey at the 6th (b18). He never got back off the bottom. Second in raw shots, last on points: handicap arithmetic, coldly applied.

rounds.angle: Jon's 41 pts and 84 gross (cr02) is the round that wins the tournament; behind him the Tour course's 15th (SI 5) takes an 11 off Patterson (b12) and a 10 off Williams (b14), and Patterson posts a course-worst 103 (cr03).

headline_candidates: Forty-Five Holes in Front — Then Along Came Alex
El Prat: The Defending Champion Remembers Himself
Mullin Slides Out of the Back of the Picture
rounds.chosen_headline: Forty-Five Holes in Front — Then Along Came Alex
rounds.angle: On TEG's first visit to El Prat, both leads change hands: Jon loses the Trophy to his brother at H13 after 45 holes in front (b01/b06) and loses the gross to Mullin at H5 (b02) before snatching it straight back at H6 (b05) — the hole where Mullin makes 7 (b18) and Mullin's Spoon fate is effectively sealed at H12 (b21).

headline_candidates: Baker Beats Baker: Six Points, and the Jacket at Last
Alex Baker's 27: A Two-Shot Lead, Dismantled
The 13th Bites Again, and It Doesn't Matter
rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Beats Baker: Six Points, and the Jacket at Last
rounds.angle: Back at the Stadium, Jon is level by H6 (b09) and gone by lunchtime of the argument: Alex's 27 pts (b11) is his worst TEG round, with an 8 at the SI 1 ninth (b19) and another at the 17th (b20); Jon's own 8 at the 13th (b16) is a footnote, and Mullin's late collapse (b39) hands over the Jacket after a level-pegging start (b22, b10).

players.arc: Jacket runner-up in three of the last four TEGs and never better than third on the Trophy in that time, he turns up in Catalonia, breaks the course record at both PGA Catalunya layouts, survives losing a 45-hole lead to his own brother, and walks off with the lot.
The defending Trophy champion is the only man to take the lead off his brother all tournament, holds it into R4 by two, and then posts 27 points — his worst TEG round — to lose by six.
Eight Jackets and counting becomes eight Jackets and stopping: new personal bests at both PGA Catalunya courses, gross runner-up by three, and dead last on points with the Spoon in his hands.
The reigning Spoon holder does everything possible to retain it — an 11 at the 15th, a course-worst 103, three quintuple bogeys — and is spared only by Mullin's late slide.
Three prior Trophy wins and a quintuple bogey in three of the four rounds, yet his R4 99 at the Stadium was fourteen shots better than his last visit here — improvement measured in wreckage avoided.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to Catalonia (the courses' prior TEG bests all date to TEG 6). Stadium bookends the tournament (R1 the 2nd TEG round here, R4 the 3rd) — use that for the bookend feel of Jon's record 90 and his closing 35 pts on the same layout. The Tour course (2nd TEG round) is the 'slightly more forgiving sibling' and duly gave up a record 84 and a course-worst 103 on the same day — worth a line. El Prat - Azul (Greg Norman, Barcelona) is a new course for TEG and is where both leads changed hands: frame it as the one unfamiliar day that reshuffled everything. Quote the cr01/cr02/cr03 record wording verbatim; do not reconcile 'prior visits' counts against the round numbering.
course_history_notes: Jon Baker's new personal bests at both PGA Catalunya courses: 90 at the Stadium in R1 (9 better than his last visit) and 84 on the Tour in R2 (6 better) — both also course records for TEG.
David Mullin's new personal bests too: 85 on the Tour in R2 (prior best 89, TEG 6) and 91 at the Stadium in R4 (prior best 94, TEG 6) — and still the Spoon.
Gregg Williams's 99 at the Stadium in R4 was 14 shots better than his last visit (113, TEG 6) — his new personal best there.
El Prat - Azul was a first visit for everyone; the fact that it produced both decisive lead changes is the point, not the yardage.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 H6 at the Stadium — Jon Baker draws level with a double bogey (b09) while Alex bleeds 7 shots in three holes (b38); Jon never trails again en route to 143 and a 6-point win.
Green Jacket: R3 H6 at El Prat — Jon Baker retakes the gross lead outright (b05) at the hole where Mullin makes 7 (b18), and holds it to the finish at +70.
Wooden Spoon: R3 H12 at El Prat — a bogey at the easiest hole on the course (SI 18) drops David Mullin to the bottom (b21), a position he never leaves.
